tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

18	1. **Find the review target.** The conversation context before this skill was triggered IS your starting point — not a blank slate. Check in this order — stop as soon as the review target is identified:
19	
20	   **Tier 1 — Explicit argument.**
21	   Did the user pass a PR, commit SHA, branch, spec file, or diff source this message?
22	   - PR reference → resolve to branch/commit via `gh pr view`. If resolution fails, ask for a SHA or branch.
23	   - Commit or branch → use directly.
24	   - Spec file → set `{spec_file}` to the provided path. Check its frontmatter for `baseline_commit`. If found, use as diff baseline. If not found, continue the cascade (a spec alone does not identify a diff source).
25	   - Also scan the argument for diff-mode keywords that narrow the scope:
26	     - "staged" / "staged changes" → Staged changes only
27	     - "uncommitted" / "working tree" / "all changes" → Uncommitted changes (staged + unstaged)
28	     - "branch diff" / "vs main" / "against main" / "compared to <branch>" → Branch diff (extract base branch if mentioned)
29	     - "commit range" / "last N commits" / "<from-sha>..<to-sha>" → Specific commit range
30	     - "this diff" / "provided diff" / "paste" → User-provided diff (do not match bare "diff" — it appears in other modes)
31	   - When multiple keywords match, prefer the most specific (e.g., "branch diff" over bare "diff").
32	
33	   **Tier 2 — Recent conversation.**
34	   Do the last few messages reveal what the user wants to be reviewed? Look for spec paths, commit refs, branches, PRs, or descriptions of a change. Apply the same diff-mode keyword scan and routing as Tier 1.
35	
36	   **Tier 3 — Sprint tracking.**
37	   Look for a sprint status file (`*sprint-status*`) in `{implementation_artifacts}` or `{planning_artifacts}`. If found, scan for stories with status `review`:
38	   - **Exactly one `review` story:** Set `{story_key}` to the story's key (e.g., `1-2-user-auth`). Suggest it: "I found story <story-id> in `review` status. Would you like to review its changes? [Y] Yes / [N] No, let me choose". If confirmed, use the story context to determine the diff source (branch name derived from story slug, or uncommitted changes). If declined, clear `{story_key}` and fall through.
39	   - **Multiple `review` stories:** Present them as numbered options alongside a manual choice option. Wait for user selection. If a story is selected, set `{story_key}` and use its context to determine the diff source. If manual choice is selected, clear `{story_key}` and fall through.
40	   - **None:** Fall through.
41	
42	   **Tier 4 — Current git state.**
43	   If version control is unavailable, skip to Tier 5. Otherwise, check the current branch and HEAD. If the branch is not `main` (or the default branch), confirm: "I see HEAD is `<short-sha>` on `<branch>` — do you want to review this branch's changes?" If confirmed, treat as a branch diff against `main`. If declined, fall through.
44	
45	   **Tier 5 — Ask.**
46	   Fall through to instruction 2.
47	
48	   Never ask extra questions beyond what the cascade prescribes. If a tier above already identified the target, skip the remaining tiers and proceed to instruction 3 (construct diff).
49	
50	2. HALT. Ask the user: **What do you want to review?** Present these options:
51	   - **Uncommitted changes** (staged + unstaged)
52	   - **Staged changes only**
53	   - **Branch diff** vs a base branch (ask which base branch)
54	   - **Specific commit range** (ask for the range)
55	   - **Provided diff or file list** (user pastes or provides a path)
56	
57	3. Construct `{diff_output}` from the chosen source.
58	   - For **staged changes only**: run `git diff --cached`.
59	   - For **uncommitted changes** (staged + unstaged): run `git diff HEAD`.
60	   - For **branch diff**: verify the base branch exists before running `git diff`. If it does not exist, HALT and ask the user for a valid branch.
61	   - For **commit range**: verify the range resolves. If it does not, HALT and ask the user for a valid range.
62	   - For **provided diff**: validate the content is non-empty and parseable as a unified diff. If it is not parseable, HALT and ask the user to provide a valid diff.
63	   - For **file list**: validate each path exists in the working tree. Construct `{diff_output}` by running `git diff HEAD -- <path1> <path2> ...`. If any paths are untracked (new files not yet staged), use `git diff --no-index /dev/null <path>` to include them. If the diff is empty (files have no uncommitted changes and are not untracked), ask the user whether to review the full file contents or to specify a different baseline.
64	   - After constructing `{diff_output}`, verify it is non-empty regardless of source type. If empty, HALT and tell the user there is nothing to review.
65	
66	4. **Set the spec context.**
67	   - If the triggering request or recent conversation **explicitly** states there is no spec (e.g. "no spec", "without a spec", "no-spec"): set `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and clear `{spec_file}` (set it to `''`). Do **not** ask for a spec. Do **not** infer no-spec mode merely because the invocation omitted a spec path.
68	   - Else if `{spec_file}` is already set (from Tier 1 or Tier 2): verify the file exists and is readable, then set `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
69	   - Else (neither a spec path nor an explicit no-spec declaration is present): ask the user to choose:
70	     1. Provide a spec or story file path for context; or
71	     2. Continue without a spec.
72	     - If the user provides a path: set `{spec_file}` to that path, verify the file exists and is readable, then set `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
73	     - If the user explicitly chooses to continue without a spec: set `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"`.
74	
75	5. If `{review_mode}` = `"full"` and the file at `{spec_file}` has a `context` field in its frontmatter listing additional docs, load each referenced document. Warn the user about any docs that cannot be found.
76	
77	6. Sanity check: if `{diff_output}` exceeds approximately 3000 lines, warn the user and offer to chunk the review by file group.
78	   - If the user opts to chunk: agree on the first group, narrow `{diff_output}` accordingly, and list the remaining groups for the user to note for follow-up runs.
79	   - If the user declines: proceed as-is with the full diff.
80	
81	### CHECKPOINT
82	
83	Present a summary before proceeding: diff stats (files changed, lines added/removed), `{review_mode}`, and loaded spec/context docs (if any). HALT and wait for user confirmation to proceed.
84	
85	## NEXT
86	
87	Read fully and follow `./step-02-review.md`
88

Launch a context-free subagent with this prompt:

Conduct a review of CONTENT.
Look for what's missing, not only what's wrong.
Find at least ten issues to fix or improve.
Output a Markdown list of findings only — no severity, priority, or ranking.
If the content is empty, stop and say so.
If you have zero findings, re-check and keep thinking; do not stop with an empty list.

CONTENT:
{diff_output}

Do not invoke any skill. Return only the review result.

"""

id = "edge-case-hunter"
name = "Edge Case Hunter"
instruction = """
Launch a context-free subagent with this prompt:

Read `{skill-root}/review-prompts/edge-case-hunter.md` completely and follow it as your review instructions.

Review content:

{diff_output}

Do not invoke any skill. If the instruction file is unreadable, report that exact failure and stop. Return only the review result.

"""

[[workflow.review_layers]]
id = "verification-gap"
name = "Verification Gap Reviewer"
instruction = """
Launch a context-free subagent with this prompt:

Read `{skill-root}/review-prompts/verification-gap.md` completely and follow it as your review instructions.

Review content:

{diff_output}

Do not invoke any skill. If the instruction file is unreadable, report that exact failure and stop. Return only the review result.

"""

id = "acceptance-auditor"
name = "Acceptance Auditor"
when = 'Only when {review_mode} = "full".'
instruction = """
Launch a subagent with this prompt:

You are an Acceptance Auditor. Review the provided diff against `{spec_file}` and any loaded context docs. Check for: violations of acceptance criteria, deviations from spec intent, missing implementation of specified behavior, contradictions between spec constraints and actual code. Output findings as a Markdown list. Each finding: one-line title, which AC/constraint it violates, and evidence from the diff.

Diff:

{diff_output}
"""

83	
84	## Design Notes
85	
86	Gaps silent in all planning docs, decided here per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed" policy:
87	- **Shared widget location:** `lib/core/widgets/` — the Structural Seed only names `core/design_tokens.dart`; this is the natural cross-feature home since Clean Architecture already lets `presentation/` depend on `core/`.
88	- **Font sourcing:** static `.ttf` files committed under `assets/fonts/` and declared in `pubspec.yaml`'s `fonts:` section — not the `google_fonts` package, which fetches at runtime by default and would make widget tests depend on network access with no device/CI yet. Fraunces and Karla ship from Google Fonts only as variable fonts (single file, `wght` axis, no static per-weight instances in the upstream repo); each is declared once per weight actually used by a typography token (`Fraunces-Variable.ttf` at weight 600; `Karla-Variable.ttf` at 400/500/700), which is Flutter's documented pattern for selecting a named instance via `TextStyle.fontWeight` — the files themselves are still fully static/offline, satisfying the "no runtime fetch" intent even though the underlying format is variable. IBM Plex Mono ships its own static `Medium` (500) instance, matching `textMonoCaption` exactly.
89	- **Epic context's "components" token category:** resolved as a handful of named constants that don't fit color/typography/spacing/radii (avatar sizes 40/52dp, default/focused-or-error border widths 1/1.5dp) — still declared inside `design_tokens.dart`, just grouped for readability.
90	- **Two colors named in prototype-extract.md §3 but outside its Design Tokens panel** (`colorChatBubbleUser` `#D9DFD3`, `colorCategoryChipText` `#3F4A38`) — added to `design_tokens.dart` now rather than left for whichever later story first renders a chat bubble or category chip, so RNF08 ("nothing is redefined or hardcoded elsewhere") holds from day one instead of being retrofitted.
91	- **Per-widget `EdgeInsets` constants** (`buttonPadding`, `textFieldContentPadding`, `avatarInitialsPadding`): not named anywhere in `prototype-extract.md` §3, but required so `lib/core/widgets/*.dart` never constructs `EdgeInsets.symmetric/all/only` directly — the Verification section's literal grep (`EdgeInsets\.(all|symmetric|only)(`) checks for the construction call itself, not just raw numbers, so these live in `design_tokens.dart` too, built from the existing spacing scale.
92	- **Disabled-state uniformity across button variants:** the Boundaries bullet and I/O matrix state the `colorBorder` background / `colorTextSecondary` text disabled rule generically ("Disabled buttons..."), and §6's component table only spells it out for the primary variant. Applied uniformly to all three variants (including secondary-outline and text-ghost, whose disabled state briefly gains a filled `colorBorder` background) for one consistent, testable rule rather than inventing a second disabled treatment for the other two.
93	- **Avatar vs. the "no fixed-height text container" rule:** the avatar circle is a fixed 40/52dp size by design (a token, not a text-driven container). It wraps its initials in a `FittedBox(fit: BoxFit.scaleDown)` so at extreme Dynamic Type scales the initials shrink to fit rather than clip or truncate — satisfying the letter of "never clips or truncates" without growing the circle itself.
94	- **Button corner radius:** `radiusSm` (8dp), applied to all three `AppButton` variants. `prototype-extract.md` §3's Radii section only names "inputs, chips" for `radiusSm` and never assigns a radius to buttons by name — buttons are the closest analog in size and visual weight to chips/inputs, so `radiusSm` was chosen over introducing an undocumented new radius value.
95	- **Pressed-state color via `overlayColor`:** `AppButton`'s primary variant resolves `ButtonStyle.overlayColor` to the exact `colorPrimaryPressed` token (opaque) on `WidgetState.pressed`, rather than relying on Material's default semi-transparent overlay tint — keeps the pressed color exact and avoids an unintended "dimmed opacity" look.

title: 'Story 1.2: Design Token System & Core Component Library'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-10-27'
status: 'done'
review_loop_iteration: 0
baseline_commit: '164e1d259a206420d612c5378adf74fefa72772c'
context:
  - '{project-root}/_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-1-context.md'
  - '{project-root}/docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md'
  - '{project-root}/_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-cerne-ciclo-b-2026-10-26/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is a typed stub (Story 1.1), and no shared, reusable UI widgets exist yet; Stories 1.3, 1.5 and 1.6 each need real colors/typography/spacing/radii and a button/text-field/avatar to build against instead of inventing their own.

**Approach:** Implement `design_tokens.dart` verbatim from `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §3, bundle the three prototype type families as static font assets, and build the three cross-feature widgets the epic names as consumed downstream (button variants, text field, avatar) in a new `lib/core/widgets/` location.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- Every color/typography/spacing/radius/elevation value in `design_tokens.dart` matches `prototype-extract.md` §3 verbatim; nothing is redefined or hardcoded elsewhere (RNF08).
- Disabled buttons render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text, never dimmed opacity; text fields expose default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
- Every widget honors Dynamic Type — no fixed-height text container that can clip or truncate.
- `core/widgets/` contains only stateless, feature-agnostic presentation primitives — no BLoC, no feature imports, no `data/`/`domain/` coupling (RNF06 applies transitively: these are consumed by every feature's `presentation/`).

**Never:**
- No component outside buttons (primary/secondary-outline/text-ghost), text field, and avatar — every other row in `prototype-extract.md` §6 (chat bubble, insight card, sync badge, filter chip, record card, confirmation dialog, PIN keypad, tab bar, waveform, skeleton, bar chart, persona/kanban cards) ships with the story that first needs it.
- No `google_fonts` runtime-fetch package — fonts are static bundled assets, so widget tests stay deterministic with no device/network (no CI exists yet).
- No extension-feature styling (persona cards, kanban) — out of scope project-wide.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Button disabled | `onPressed == null` | `colorBorder` background, `colorTextSecondary` text, no ripple/pressed feedback | N/A |
| Text field error | `errorText != null` | 1.5px `colorError` border, error text shown below field | N/A |
| Dynamic Type max scale | System text-scale increased | Label wraps/grows; never clips or truncates | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- placeholder stub to replace with real `colors`/`typography`/`spacing`/`radii`/`elevation` constants (currently just a doc comment pointing here).
- `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §3 (tokens) and §6 (component table) -- read-only ground truth for every literal value and the exact variations each widget must support.
- `pubspec.yaml` -- add a `fonts:` section + `assets/fonts/` entries for Fraunces, Karla, IBM Plex Mono (no such section exists today; only `.env` is declared as an asset).
- `lib/core/widgets/` -- new directory; architecture spine's Structural Seed is silent on where cross-feature shared widgets live (only `core/design_tokens.dart` is named) — decided here per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed" policy, analogous placement to `core/design_tokens.dart`.
- `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-1-context.md` Cross-Story Dependencies -- names exactly this story's output (tokens + buttons/text fields/avatar) as what 1.3/1.5/1.6 consume; do not expand scope beyond it.
- `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-1-1-project-scaffold-stack-integration-core-infrastructure.md` Design Notes -- precedent pattern for documenting a decided silent-gap.

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` -- implement real color/typography/spacing/radii/elevation constants verbatim from `prototype-extract.md` §3 -- RNF08 single source of truth
- [x] `assets/fonts/*` + `pubspec.yaml` -- bundle Fraunces/Karla/IBM Plex Mono as static font assets -- deterministic text rendering with no device/CI
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart` -- primary, secondary (outline), text (ghost) variants with the disabled-state rule -- consumed by 1.3/1.5/1.6
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/app_text_field.dart` -- default/focused/error border states -- consumed by 1.3
- [x] `lib/core/widgets/avatar.dart` -- initials circle, 40px and 52px size variants -- consumed by 1.6 and Epic 8
- [x] `test/core/widgets/app_button_test.dart`, `app_text_field_test.dart`, `avatar_test.dart` -- cover every visual state listed in the I/O matrix and §6
- [x] `test/core/design_tokens_test.dart` -- spot-check token values against `prototype-extract.md` §3

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given any token category, when read from `design_tokens.dart`, then its value matches `prototype-extract.md` §3 verbatim.
- Given a repo-wide search for color/font/spacing/radius literals outside `design_tokens.dart`, then none exist (RNF08).
- Given the disabled button state, when rendered, then background is `colorBorder` and text is `colorTextSecondary`.
- Given the text field error state, when rendered, then the border is 1.5px `colorError`.
- Given increased system Dynamic Type scale, when any of the three widgets render, then no label clips or truncates.

### Review Findings

- [x] [Review][Patch] Remove unreachable `disabledBorder` in `AppTextField` — no `enabled` param exists to ever trigger it [lib/core/widgets/app_text_field.dart:81]
- [x] [Review][Patch] Run `dart format` on the three new widget files — not formatter-clean as committed [lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart, lib/core/widgets/app_text_field.dart, lib/core/widgets/avatar.dart]
- [x] [Review][Defer] `AppButton` has no loading/busy state for async call sites (login submit, "Salvar", export actions) [lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] `AppTextField` lacks `enabled`/`readOnly`/`onSubmitted`/`autofocus`/`textCapitalization`/`inputFormatters` — first real consumer (Story 1.3) should request what it needs [lib/core/widgets/app_text_field.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] `design_tokens.dart` now imports `package:flutter/widgets.dart` with no lint/architecture test guarding a future `domain/` layer from importing it (RNF06 risk) [lib/core/design_tokens.dart:1] — deferred, pre-existing

## Spec Change Log

- **Review round 1 (patch findings, no spec-level change):** three parallel reviews (blind-hunter, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap) surfaced 6 distinct patchable gaps, all fixed in place: (1) added a `DesignTokens — layout insets` test group for `buttonPadding`/`textFieldContentPadding`/`avatarInitialsPadding`, previously untested; (2) added a `side.resolve({disabled})` assertion to `AppButton`'s secondaryOutline disabled test; (3) `AppButton.secondaryOutline`'s `BorderSide` now passes `width: DesignTokens.borderWidthDefault` explicitly instead of silently falling back to Flutter's default (RNF08 literal bypass); (4) documented the button-corner-radius decision below (was undocumented); (5) corrected `AppTextField.errorText`'s doc comment, which overstated the contract ("non-null and non-empty") beyond the frozen spec's actual `errorText != null` condition; (6) added `radiusSm` assertions to the `AppButton` primary and `AppTextField` default-state tests. Rejected as non-issues: `textColor` no-op on non-ghost variants (documented by design), `Avatar` empty-initials fallback (caller's responsibility per its own doc), missing pressed-overlay on secondary/ghost (prototype never defines one), barrel file/a11y/form-hooks suggestions (deferred or out of scope, see `deferred-work.md`).

## Design Notes

Gaps silent in all planning docs, decided here per AGENTS.md's "decide and proceed" policy:
- **Shared widget location:** `lib/core/widgets/` — the Structural Seed only names `core/design_tokens.dart`; this is the natural cross-feature home since Clean Architecture already lets `presentation/` depend on `core/`.
- **Font sourcing:** static `.ttf` files committed under `assets/fonts/` and declared in `pubspec.yaml`'s `fonts:` section — not the `google_fonts` package, which fetches at runtime by default and would make widget tests depend on network access with no device/CI yet. Fraunces and Karla ship from Google Fonts only as variable fonts (single file, `wght` axis, no static per-weight instances in the upstream repo); each is declared once per weight actually used by a typography token (`Fraunces-Variable.ttf` at weight 600; `Karla-Variable.ttf` at 400/500/700), which is Flutter's documented pattern for selecting a named instance via `TextStyle.fontWeight` — the files themselves are still fully static/offline, satisfying the "no runtime fetch" intent even though the underlying format is variable. IBM Plex Mono ships its own static `Medium` (500) instance, matching `textMonoCaption` exactly.
- **Epic context's "components" token category:** resolved as a handful of named constants that don't fit color/typography/spacing/radii (avatar sizes 40/52dp, default/focused-or-error border widths 1/1.5dp) — still declared inside `design_tokens.dart`, just grouped for readability.
- **Two colors named in prototype-extract.md §3 but outside its Design Tokens panel** (`colorChatBubbleUser` `#D9DFD3`, `colorCategoryChipText` `#3F4A38`) — added to `design_tokens.dart` now rather than left for whichever later story first renders a chat bubble or category chip, so RNF08 ("nothing is redefined or hardcoded elsewhere") holds from day one instead of being retrofitted.
- **Per-widget `EdgeInsets` constants** (`buttonPadding`, `textFieldContentPadding`, `avatarInitialsPadding`): not named anywhere in `prototype-extract.md` §3, but required so `lib/core/widgets/*.dart` never constructs `EdgeInsets.symmetric/all/only` directly — the Verification section's literal grep (`EdgeInsets\.(all|symmetric|only)(`) checks for the construction call itself, not just raw numbers, so these live in `design_tokens.dart` too, built from the existing spacing scale.
- **Disabled-state uniformity across button variants:** the Boundaries bullet and I/O matrix state the `colorBorder` background / `colorTextSecondary` text disabled rule generically ("Disabled buttons..."), and §6's component table only spells it out for the primary variant. Applied uniformly to all three variants (including secondary-outline and text-ghost, whose disabled state briefly gains a filled `colorBorder` background) for one consistent, testable rule rather than inventing a second disabled treatment for the other two.
- **Avatar vs. the "no fixed-height text container" rule:** the avatar circle is a fixed 40/52dp size by design (a token, not a text-driven container). It wraps its initials in a `FittedBox(fit: BoxFit.scaleDown)` so at extreme Dynamic Type scales the initials shrink to fit rather than clip or truncate — satisfying the letter of "never clips or truncates" without growing the circle itself.
- **Button corner radius:** `radiusSm` (8dp), applied to all three `AppButton` variants. `prototype-extract.md` §3's Radii section only names "inputs, chips" for `radiusSm` and never assigns a radius to buttons by name — buttons are the closest analog in size and visual weight to chips/inputs, so `radiusSm` was chosen over introducing an undocumented new radius value.
- **Pressed-state color via `overlayColor`:** `AppButton`'s primary variant resolves `ButtonStyle.overlayColor` to the exact `colorPrimaryPressed` token (opaque) on `WidgetState.pressed`, rather than relying on Material's default semi-transparent overlay tint — keeps the pressed color exact and avoids an unintended "dimmed opacity" look.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter pub get` -- resolves with the new font assets declared, no conflicts
- `fvm flutter test` -- all new token/widget tests pass
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- zero issues
- `grep -rn "Color(0x\|fontSize:\|EdgeInsets\.\(all\|symmetric\|only\)(" lib --include=*.dart | grep -v "core/design_tokens.dart"` -- expected: no matches (RNF08 literal check)

## Suggested Review Order

**Design tokens (RNF08 single source)**

- Entry point: every color/typography/spacing/radii/elevation constant, transcribed verbatim from the prototype panel.
  [`design_tokens.dart:10`](../../lib/core/design_tokens.dart#L10)
- "Components" and "Layout insets" groups are the two categories the prototype leaves unnamed — decided here, documented below.
  [`design_tokens.dart:195`](../../lib/core/design_tokens.dart#L195)
- Font assets bundled statically (not `google_fonts`) so widget tests stay deterministic with no device/CI.
  [`pubspec.yaml:106`](../../pubspec.yaml#L106)

**AppButton (shared primitive, three variants)**

- Variant switch — primary/secondaryOutline/textGhost share one disabled rule, diverge on fill/outline/ghost styling.
  [`app_button.dart:54`](../../lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart#L54)
- Patched post-review: `secondaryOutline`'s border now reads `borderWidthDefault` explicitly instead of silently defaulting to 1.0.
  [`app_button.dart:97`](../../lib/core/widgets/app_button.dart#L97)

**AppTextField (border states)**

- Default/focused/error borders resolved from tokens; patched post-review to correct a doc comment that overstated the error contract.
  [`app_text_field.dart:31`](../../lib/core/widgets/app_text_field.dart#L31)
- `errorMaxLines: null` — the Dynamic Type boundary: long error text wraps instead of truncating.
  [`app_text_field.dart:69`](../../lib/core/widgets/app_text_field.dart#L69)

**Avatar (fixed-size + Dynamic Type)**

- `FittedBox` shrinks initials to fit a fixed-size circle under extreme text scales, rather than growing the circle.
  [`avatar.dart:40`](../../lib/core/widgets/avatar.dart#L40)

**Tests (peripherals)**

- Token values spot-checked against the prototype extract, including the post-review layout-insets group.
  [`design_tokens_test.dart:1`](../../test/core/design_tokens_test.dart#L1)
- Every I/O-matrix row (disabled button, text-field error, Dynamic Type) covered per widget, plus the post-review disabled-border assertion.
  [`app_button_test.dart:1`](../../test/core/widgets/app_button_test.dart#L1)
- [`app_text_field_test.dart:1`](../../test/core/widgets/app_text_field_test.dart#L1)
- [`avatar_test.dart:1`](../../test/core/widgets/avatar_test.dart#L1)

1	# Epic 1 Context: Foundation & Session Management
2	
3	<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	This epic delivers the scaffold every other feature depends on: the pinned-stack project setup with its core infrastructure verified working together, the full visual design-token system, email/password authentication with silent session refresh, the session-expiry recovery overlay, and a base navigation shell with placeholders for everything not yet built. It is delivered first because every later epic assumes this foundation — DI, networking, error handling, session state, design tokens, and navigation — already exists and is stable. Users come away able to create an account, log in, stay logged in across restarts, recover gracefully if their session expires mid-use, and navigate the whole app shell even though most feature screens are still placeholders.
8	
9	## Stories
10	
11	- Story 1.1: Project Scaffold, Stack Integration & Core Infrastructure
12	- Story 1.2: Design Token System & Core Component Library
13	- Story 1.3: Account Creation and Login
14	- Story 1.4: Silent Session Refresh & Persistence
15	- Story 1.5: Expired-Session Recovery Overlay
16	- Story 1.6: Base Navigation Shell with Feature Placeholders
17	
18	## Requirements & Constraints
19	
20	- Account creation and login round-trip through the backend with exactly two fields (email, password) — no password confirmation, no display-name field at signup. Login/signup/refresh are the only calls using the anon key; every other call uses the user's access token.
21	- A valid, unexpired session must persist across app restarts with no re-prompt; nearing/past-expiry sessions refresh silently with no visible loading UI unless the call exceeds 300ms.
22	- When the backend reports an expired session, an overlay appears over whatever screen is active (never a navigation away); the underlying screen's state/scroll position is preserved; "Entrar novamente" leads to biometric/PIN re-auth, not a login form.
23	- All four base destinations (Home/Chat, side menu, Meus Registros, Configurações) must be reachable from launch; any destination whose feature isn't built yet shows a visually distinct, fully-polished placeholder — never a broken link and never a visibly "unfinished" look.
24	- Local UI interactions must respond in <100ms; any network call >300ms shows a loading indicator (manual timing spot-check, no automated perf tooling).
25	- Zero Clean Architecture layer violations: domain imports neither Flutter nor anything from a data layer.
26	- ≥80% domain-layer test coverage; the write-failure matrix (5 write endpoints × 3 failure types: timeout, malformed response, no connection = 15 scenarios) must be fully handled with zero unhandled exceptions — this epic builds the one shared, reusable test helper every later feature's write-endpoint tests reuse.
27	- Zero hardcoded visual values outside the design-tokens file; every control must honor Dynamic Type without truncating.
28	- An integration spike, before any other building, must prove `dio` + `flutter_secure_storage` + `get_it` work together in one bootstrap — this combination is otherwise unverified.
29	
30	## Technical Decisions
31	
32	- Single DI container: exactly one `get_it` instance registered at bootstrap; `dio` is configured through it; secrets (`FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) load via `flutter_dotenv` from a gitignored `.env`, never hardcoded.
33	- One sealed `Failure` hierarchy, exactly 14 subtypes (13 from the backend's error taxonomy plus a local-only `MalformedResponse`), defined once and never redefined/subset per feature; every repository method returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (or a `Stream` for SSE), with no native/dio exception ever escaping unmapped.
34	- One retry interceptor on the `dio`/`ApiClient` layer retries only the 6 server-marked `retryable:true` codes; every other failure surfaces once, unretried.
35	- One URL builder maps every operation to `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<x-cerne-function>/<path-params>` (never the literal OpenAPI REST path); one interceptor owns headers — `apikey` on every call, anon-key bearer token only on signup/login/refresh, user access token on everything else.
36	- Exactly one `SessionStatus` stream is exposed from the auth feature's domain layer and registered once in DI as a singleton; every later consumer (including RF07/Epic 4) injects/listens to it rather than re-deriving session validity from a raw 401 or a second stream.
37	- This epic builds the `go_router` redirect skeleton composing session state; Epic 2 (RF03) later plugs a local vault-status gate into the same redirect, checked before session status — this epic should leave that composition point open rather than hardcoding a session-only redirect.
38	- Strict layer direction applies project-wide: only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any feature's `data/` directly; a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency.
39	- Structural seed to scaffold: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for `data/domain/presentation`.
40	- Full stack is pinned (Flutter 3.47.x via `fvm`; `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `dio`, `hive_ce`, `get_it`, `fpdart`, `freezed`, `json_serializable`, `mocktail`, `fl_chart`, `local_auth`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv`, `whisper_ggml` — exact versions in the architecture spine's stack-pins table) and must resolve with no conflicts before anything else is built.
41	- Design tokens (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`, plus the two elevation constants) are implemented verbatim, camelCase, as the single source of truth; every other file reads from them, never redefines a value.
42	
43	## UX & Interaction Patterns
44	
45	- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.
46	- Buttons and text fields come from one shared component set: disabled buttons always render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text (never dimmed opacity); text fields show distinct default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
47	- The side menu is the sole navigation hub (plus back arrows and sheet "x" closes) — no drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar. It must resolve all four destinations (chat session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, Planos de Ação) without a 404 or crash.
48	- The Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit, never-implemented extension feature) must still look fully finished — same visual polish as real screens, no graying-out, no backend calls, no drag/drop logic.
49	- The avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is built here for reuse, not reimplementation, when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (Epic 8).
50	- The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (`colorTextPrimary`) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides `sheetUp` for bottom sheets.
51	- Copy for the overlay must avoid any language implying data loss or starting over; history and scroll position are understood by the user to be preserved.
52	
53	## Cross-Story Dependencies
54	
55	- Story 1.1 (DI, API client, Failure hierarchy, URL builder, retry interceptor, shared failure-matrix test helper) is a hard prerequisite for every other story in this epic and for every later epic's write-endpoint tests.
56	- Story 1.2's design tokens and base components (buttons, text fields, avatar) are consumed by Story 1.3's login/signup screen, Story 1.5's overlay, and Story 1.6's navigation shell/placeholders.
57	- Story 1.4 depends on Story 1.3's auth calls and exposes the singleton `SessionStatus` stream that Story 1.5 listens to and that the `go_router` redirect skeleton composes.
58	- Story 1.5's "Entrar novamente" action routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow that is not built until Epic 2 — this epic should wire the route target without implementing that flow.
59	- Story 1.6's `go_router` redirect skeleton is extended by Epic 2 (RF03), which plugs in the local vault-status gate ahead of the session gate already built here, in a fixed order (vault checked first).
60	- Story 1.6's avatar component and placeholder-styling pattern are reused as-is by Epic 8 (Configurações' 52px avatar, other placeholder surfaces).
61

- Strict layer direction applies project-wide: only `data/` imports `dio`/`hive_ce`/platform plugins; `presentation/` never imports any feature's `data/` directly; a BLoC/Cubit constructor never takes another BLoC/Cubit as a dependency.
- Structural seed to scaffold: `lib/core/{design_tokens.dart, network/, failure/, di/, cache/, resource.dart, isolated_side_effect.dart, session/}` and `lib/features/{auth, vault, entries, capture, chat, export, dashboard, account}/`, each pre-wired for `data/domain/presentation`.
- Full stack is pinned (Flutter 3.47.x via `fvm`; `flutter_bloc`, `go_router`, `dio`, `hive_ce`, `get_it`, `fpdart`, `freezed`, `json_serializable`, `mocktail`, `fl_chart`, `local_auth`, `flutter_secure_storage`, `flutter_dotenv`, `whisper_ggml` — exact versions in the architecture spine's stack-pins table) and must resolve with no conflicts before anything else is built.
- Design tokens (`colors`, `typography`, `rounded`, `spacing`, `components`, plus the two elevation constants) are implemented verbatim, camelCase, as the single source of truth; every other file reads from them, never redefines a value.

## UX & Interaction Patterns

- Single fixed frame: 390×844 logical points, portrait only, light mode only — no breakpoint, landscape, or dark-mode path anywhere in the app.
- Buttons and text fields come from one shared component set: disabled buttons always render `colorBorder` background + `colorTextSecondary` text (never dimmed opacity); text fields show distinct default/focused(`colorPrimary`, 1.5px)/error(`colorError`) border states.
- The side menu is the sole navigation hub (plus back arrows and sheet "x" closes) — no drawer-within-drawer, no tab bar. It must resolve all four destinations (chat session switching, Meus Registros, Configurações, Planos de Ação) without a 404 or crash.
- The Planos de Ação placeholder (an explicit, never-implemented extension feature) must still look fully finished — same visual polish as real screens, no graying-out, no backend calls, no drag/drop logic.
- The avatar component (solid `colorPrimary` circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, 40px) is built here for reuse, not reimplementation, when Configurações needs its 52px variant later (Epic 8).
- The "Sessão expirada" overlay is a scrim over the current screen using the confirmation-dialog component with a neutral (`colorTextPrimary`) title — never the red destructive-title variant. It traps focus until dismissed/actioned, is the only overlay allowed on screen at a time (never stacks on another open overlay), and its entrance uses only the `scrimIn` (0.18s) choreography — no other motion exists in the system besides `sheetUp` for bottom sheets.
- Copy for the overlay must avoid any language implying data loss or starting over; history and scroll position are understood by the user to be preserved.

## Cross-Story Dependencies

- Story 1.1 (DI, API client, Failure hierarchy, URL builder, retry interceptor, shared failure-matrix test helper) is a hard prerequisite for every other story in this epic and for every later epic's write-endpoint tests.
- Story 1.2's design tokens and base components (buttons, text fields, avatar) are consumed by Story 1.3's login/signup screen, Story 1.5's overlay, and Story 1.6's navigation shell/placeholders.
- Story 1.4 depends on Story 1.3's auth calls and exposes the singleton `SessionStatus` stream that Story 1.5 listens to and that the `go_router` redirect skeleton composes.
- Story 1.5's "Entrar novamente" action routes to the biometric/PIN re-auth flow that is not built until Epic 2 — this epic should wire the route target without implementing that flow.
- Story 1.6's `go_router` redirect skeleton is extended by Epic 2 (RF03), which plugs in the local vault-status gate ahead of the session gate already built here, in a fixed order (vault checked first).
- Story 1.6's avatar component and placeholder-styling pattern are reused as-is by Epic 8 (Configurações' 52px avatar, other placeholder surfaces).

187	- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
188	- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
189	- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
190	- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.
191	
192	---
193	
194	## 5. Implementation notes
195	
196	1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
197	2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
198	3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
199	4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
200	5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
201	6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
202	7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.
203	
204	---
205	
206	## 6. Component library
207	
208	| Component | Where it appears | Variations |
209	|---|---|---|
210	| Primary button | Auth, modals, sheets, confirmations | normal (`#1F3D34`) · pressed (`#16281F`, darker) · disabled (`#E1DACB` background, `#6B6255` text) |
211	| Secondary button (outline) | "Tentar novamente", "Cancelar", "Baixar dados brutos" | `#1F3D34` outline, no fill |
212	| Text button (ghost) | Mode-toggle links, "Fechar", "Limpar" | no background, `#1F3D34` or `#6B6255` depending on context |
213	| Text field | Login, Texto tab, name editing | empty · focused (1.5px `#1F3D34` border) · error (`#B3402A` border) |
214	| Chat bubble | Home/Chat | user (light green, straight bottom-right corner) · AI (ivory with shadow, straight bottom-left corner) · streaming (pulsing cursor at the end of the text) |
215	| Insight card | Home/Chat | ochre spine, mono label "INSIGHT", dismiss button |
216	| Bookmark button (RF10) | User messages in the chat | idle (outline) · saving (spinner) · saved (ochre check) · error (red warning) |
217	| Send-error banner | Home/Chat | "Não foi possível enviar — toque para tentar novamente"; background `rgba(179,64,42,.08)`, warning icon, red text |
218	| Offline banner | Home/Chat | blue-gray background `#5C7A93`, `ph-wifi-slash` icon, light text |
219	| Sync badge | Record cards (Tela 4) | synced (green dot) · synchronizing (ochre dot) · sync error (red dot) |
220	| Filter chip | Filter sheet, active filters | single choice (date) · multiple choice (category, type) · removable with "x" (active filters) |
221	| Record card | Tela 4 | spine colored by origin (manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre) |
222	| Kanban card **[ext]** | Planos de Ação | spine by column (to do / in progress / done) |
223	| Initials avatar | Side menu, Configurações | dark green circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, two sizes (40px in the menu, 52px in Configurações) |
224	| AI persona card **[ext]** | Configurações | not selected (thin border) · selected (thick `#1F3D34` border + check icon) |
225	| Bar chart (dashboard) | Configurações | populated (10 bars) · one bar · empty (placeholder icon) |
226	| Export status card | Tela 4 (bottom sheet) | pending · processing · done · error · empty |
227	| Confirmation dialog | Sessão expirada, Confirmar exclusão | background scrim + centered card; neutral title (session) or red title (destructive deletion) |
228	| PIN keypad | Tela 0.1b/c | digits 0–9 + backspace; progress dots above |
229	| Tab bar | Insertion modal | 3 tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto), active tab with filled background |
230	| Audio waveform | Insertion modal, Áudio tab | active/animated (recording) · frozen and faded (processing) |

  ├─ empty state (no records) ──CTA "Criar primeiro registro"──> Insertion modal
  ├─ overlay: filter sheet ──"Aplicar"──> active filters (chips on the list)
  └─ overlay: export card (download icon) ──> pending ──> processing ──> done | error | empty period

Planos de Ação (base screen, from the side menu) — static screen, 3-column kanban (extension, not implemented)

Configurações (base screen, from the side menu)
  ├─ dashboard variations: zero entries | one entry | more than 30 (with narrative) | narrative unavailable
  ├─ inline profile-name editing
  ├─ AI persona selection (Analítico / Empático / Socrático) (extension, not implemented)
  ├─ "Sair" ──> Biometria
  └─ overlay: account-deletion confirmation ──"Apagar tudo"──> Biometria (same destination as logout)
```

---

## 2. Navigable states

Names as they appear in the prototype. The prototype's own state catalog has 32 entries: Tela 0 — Splash; Tela 0.1 — Biometria; Tela 0.1a — Entrar / criar conta; Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial; Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha; Tela 1 — Home / Chat; Tela 2 — Texto, Áudio (Gravando, Processando, Transcrito, Erro), Foto (Captura, Processando OCR, Reconhecido, Erro); Tela 3 — Menu lateral; Tela 1 — Sessão expirada; Tela 4 — Meus Registros, Estado vazio, Sheet de filtro, Filtros ativos; Exportar — Pendente, Processando, Concluído, Erro, Período vazio; Tela 5 — Planos de Ação **[ext]**; Tela 6 — Configurações, Dashboard zero entradas, Dashboard uma entrada, Narrativa indisponível, Confirmar exclusão. The tables below group them by screen; some rows describe variations inside one state (e.g., the bookmark sub-states, the streaming response). Extension states (requirements, section 2) are marked **[ext]**.

### 2.1 Entry and authentication
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 0 — Splash | Wordmark "Cerne" centered on dark green, 3 loading dots; lasts 1.8 s and moves on automatically. |
| Tela 0.1 — Biometria | Fingerprint circle, title "Toque para desbloquear", link "Usar PIN", secondary link "usar e-mail e senha" near the bottom. |
| Tela 0.1a — Entrar | Login mode: title "Bem-vindo de volta", fields E-mail and Senha, CTA "Entrar", toggle link, link "usar biometria". |
| Tela 0.1a — Criar conta | Same screen in sign-up mode: title "Crie sua conta", CTA "Criar conta" (toggled by a text link, not a separate screen). |
| Tela 0.1b — PIN inicial | Title "Digite seu PIN", 4 progress dots, 3×4 numeric keypad with backspace; after the 4th digit, moves on after 350 ms. |
| Tela 0.1c — PIN após falha | Same as 0.1b plus the error band "Não foi possível reconhecer — digite seu PIN". |

### 2.2 Conversation
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 1 — Home/Chat (default) | Messages going back and forth; dark green fixed header with ☰ and wordmark; composer with "+", placeholder "Escreva uma mensagem...", send icon. |
| Tela 1 — Streaming | AI response revealed progressively with a pulsing cursor. |
| Tela 1 — Insight | Insight card with ochre spine, label "INSIGHT", "x" to dismiss, interleaved in the messages. |
| Tela 1 — Falha ao gerar resposta | Incomplete AI message with "Falha ao gerar resposta — toque para tentar novamente" in red, in place of the time. |
| Tela 1 — Bookmark | Bookmark on each user message with 4 sub-states: `idle`, `saving` (spinner), `saved` (ochre check), `error` (red warning). |
| Tela 1 — Offline | Blue-gray banner "Sem conexão — histórico disponível, novas mensagens bloqueadas"; send icon disabled. |
| Tela 1 — Sessão expirada | Light scrim over the chat (still readable), centered card with lock icon, title "Sessão expirada", text saying history and scroll position are kept, button "Entrar novamente". |
| Tela 3 — Menu lateral | Drawer: initials avatar and name; section "CONVERSAS" with past sessions (title + timestamp); items "Meus Registros", "Planos de Ação", "Configurações"; new-conversation action. |

### 2.3 Insertion modal (bottom sheet over Home/Chat; 9 states)
Common structure: "x" to close and a 3-tab bar (Texto / Áudio / Foto); the active tab has a filled dark-green background.

| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Texto | Multiline field, placeholder "Escreva livremente...", button "Salvar". |
| Áudio — Gravando | Red stop button, animated 12-bar waveform, monospace timer (e.g., "00:12"). |
| Áudio — Processando | Spinner in place of stop; frozen, faded waveform (opacity .35); text "Transcrevendo..."; label "00:42 de áudio". |
| Áudio — Transcrito | Editable transcribed text; original audio duration in mono; "Salvar" enabled. |
| Áudio — Erro | Red warning icon, "Não foi possível transcrever", outline button "Tentar novamente". |
| Foto — Captura | Two large buttons, "Câmera" and "Galeria". |
| Foto — Processando OCR | Photo thumbnail, spinner, "Reconhecendo texto...". |
| Foto — Reconhecido | Small thumbnail next to the extracted (editable) text; "Salvar". |
| Foto — Erro | Thumbnail kept, warning icon, "Não foi possível reconhecer o texto", button "Tentar novamente" and secondary text action "Salvar só a foto". |

### 2.4 Records
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tela 4 — Meus Registros (default) | Records grouped by date ("Hoje", "Ontem", dates); each card with a spine colored by origin, source icon, time, sync indicator (green "sincronizado" / ochre "sincronizando" / red "erro de sync"), text excerpt, category chips when present; header with back arrow, title, download icon; search bar "Buscar nos registros..." with a funnel button. |
| Tela 4 — Vazio | Large notebook icon, "Nenhum registro ainda", CTA "Criar primeiro registro". |
| Tela 4 — Filtros ativos | Removable chips under the search bar with the applied filters, link "Limpar filtros"; funnel button filled. |
| Tela 4 — Sheet de filtro | Groups "INTERVALO DE DATA" (Todo o período / Esta semana / Este mês, single choice), "CATEGORIA" (chips: trabalho, rotina, descanso, relações), "TIPO DE ENTRADA" (chips: manual, áudio, foto, chat); "Aplicar" and "Limpar". **Note:** the backend has no category filter (requirements, RF06); categories are the tags extension. |

### 2.5 Export (bottom sheet over Tela 4; 5 states)
| State | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Pendente | Spinner, "Preparando exportação...". |
| Processando | "Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar. |
| Concluído | Green check, "Resumo pronto", buttons "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline). |
| Erro | Red warning; text explaining that the AI narrative failed but the data remains available; only the button "Baixar dados brutos". |
| Período vazio | "Nenhum registro nesse período." and a suggestion to adjust the filter; no download button. |

All five have the link "Fechar" at the bottom. The mapping between these states and the backend job statuses is in `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`.

| State | What it shows |

Other elements of Configurações: avatar with editable name/e-mail (pencil becomes a check in edit mode — inline editing); persona cards "Como a IA responde" (Analítico, Empático, Socrático) **[ext]**; actions "Sair" and "Apagar conta" (red).

---

## 3. Visual system (tokens for `design_tokens.dart`)

The prototype has a **Design Tokens** panel, marked as the ground truth for `design_tokens.dart`. Its names and values are below.

### Colors

| `colorPrimary` | `#1F3D34` | Buttons, app bar, wordmark |

| `colorInfoOffline` | `#5C7A93` | Offline banner — single use |

Other colors that appear on specific screens but not in the panel: user chat bubble `#D9DFD3`; text on category chips `#3F4A38`.

### Typography
| Token | Font · weight · size/line-height | Use |

| `textDisplayLg` | Fraunces 600 · 32/38 | Splash wordmark |
| `textHeadlineMd` | Fraunces 600 · 24/30 | Section titles |

### Spacing (4 dp grid)
`spacingXs` 4 · `spacingSm` 8 · `spacingMd` 16 · `spacingLg` 24 · `spacingXl` 32 · `spacing2xl` 48 (dp).

### Radii
`radiusSm` 8 dp (inputs, chips) · `radiusMd` 16 dp (cards, bubbles) · `radiusLg` 24 dp (sheets, modals) · `radiusFull` 999 dp (avatars, pills).

### Elevation
`elevation1` — `0 1px 3px rgba(36,31,25,.08)` (cards at rest) · `elevation2` — `0 4px 16px rgba(36,31,25,.14)` (sheets, modals).

### Icons
Phosphor library, Regular style, 24 dp: `list`, `plus`, `magnifying-glass`, `funnel`, `bookmark-simple`, `microphone`, `camera`, `gear`, `kanban`, `notebook`, `fingerprint`, `lightbulb` (and others used on specific screens: `check`, `warning-circle`, `wifi-slash`, `circle-notch`, `caret-left`, `download-simple`, `pencil-simple`, `x`, `stop`, `image`, `check-circle`, `chart-line-up`, `backspace`, `lock-key`, `paper-plane-tilt`, `chat-circle-text`).

### Spine (colored bar on the left of a card) — 3 contexts
1. Proactive insight in the chat — ochre.
2. Entry origin in "Meus Registros" — color by type: manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre.
3. Kanban column in "Planos de Ação" — color by column **[ext]**.

### Micro-animations and transitions
- `scrimIn` (0.18 s ease-out): fade of the darkened background when any overlay opens.
- `sheetUp` (0.2 s ease-out): bottom sheets (insertion modal, filter, export) rise from the bottom of the screen.
- Continuous spinner (`spin`, 1 s linear infinite) in every loading state.
- Text streaming: the AI response is revealed progressively, with a blinking cursor at the end while it is "typing".
- PIN: after the 4th digit, a 350 ms pause before navigating.

---

## 4. Special states that need extra care

- **Expired session:** an overlay on the chat that keeps history and scroll position — the expired token must not discard the conversation state in memory before re-authentication. Re-authenticating goes back to the Biometria screen, not to a full form.
- **Offline:** blocks **sending new messages** (send icon disabled, explanatory banner), but **history stays visible and navigable**. The prototype does not show what happens to the insertion modal (text/audio/photo) when offline.
- **Asynchronous processing — audio transcription:** a loading state (spinner + frozen waveform) and two outcomes (success/error); the error always offers "Tentar novamente" and never loses the recorded audio.
- **Asynchronous processing — photo OCR:** same pattern as audio, with one extra exit on error: "Salvar só a foto", which saves the record even without extracted text.
- **Asynchronous processing — export:** two loading stages (preparing → generating the AI summary) before the result; on error, the raw data is always available for download — the failure is isolated to the AI narrative, never to the user's data.
- **Dashboard narrative unavailable:** the chart loads normally but the AI summary paragraph fails — distinct from "zero entries" (lack of data) and needs its own error message.

---

## 5. Implementation notes

1. **"29 frames" vs. "32 states":** the prototype has 32 distinct navigable states, but the number of frames (29) suggests that some state families should be one screen with internal state, not separate routes (e.g., a single `ExportSheet` with a status enum instead of 5 routes). Consider this when designing navigation.
2. **Account deletion without a success screen:** both "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" return to the Biometria screen; there is no "account deleted" or "you signed out" screen.
3. **Login vs. sign-up:** the same screen toggled by a text link; the prototype shows no extra sign-up fields (e.g., password confirmation, name). Whether sign-up needs extra fields is a product decision not covered visually.
4. **Insertion modal when offline:** not represented.
5. **Switching tabs in the insertion modal:** opening the modal always resets every tab to `idle`/empty, but switching tabs *during* a modal session is not cleared automatically — the expected behavior (e.g., whether an ongoing recording is discarded on tab switch) is not defined by the prototype.
6. **Per-entry sync indicator:** the states "sincronizado / sincronizando / erro de sync" exist visually on the cards, but no explicit "retry sync" action is shown for the error state. The semantics of the badge are in `docs/input/backend/sync-badge.md`.
7. **Text search combined with filters:** the filter sheet and the text search are on the same screen, but the prototype does not show them acting together.

---

## 6. Component library

| Component | Where it appears | Variations |
|---|---|---|
| Primary button | Auth, modals, sheets, confirmations | normal (`#1F3D34`) · pressed (`#16281F`, darker) · disabled (`#E1DACB` background, `#6B6255` text) |
| Secondary button (outline) | "Tentar novamente", "Cancelar", "Baixar dados brutos" | `#1F3D34` outline, no fill |
| Text button (ghost) | Mode-toggle links, "Fechar", "Limpar" | no background, `#1F3D34` or `#6B6255` depending on context |
| Text field | Login, Texto tab, name editing | empty · focused (1.5px `#1F3D34` border) · error (`#B3402A` border) |
| Chat bubble | Home/Chat | user (light green, straight bottom-right corner) · AI (ivory with shadow, straight bottom-left corner) · streaming (pulsing cursor at the end of the text) |
| Insight card | Home/Chat | ochre spine, mono label "INSIGHT", dismiss button |
| Bookmark button (RF10) | User messages in the chat | idle (outline) · saving (spinner) · saved (ochre check) · error (red warning) |
| Send-error banner | Home/Chat | "Não foi possível enviar — toque para tentar novamente"; background `rgba(179,64,42,.08)`, warning icon, red text |
| Offline banner | Home/Chat | blue-gray background `#5C7A93`, `ph-wifi-slash` icon, light text |
| Sync badge | Record cards (Tela 4) | synced (green dot) · synchronizing (ochre dot) · sync error (red dot) |
| Filter chip | Filter sheet, active filters | single choice (date) · multiple choice (category, type) · removable with "x" (active filters) |
| Record card | Tela 4 | spine colored by origin (manual = dark green, audio = olive green, photo = gray, chat = ochre) |
| Kanban card **[ext]** | Planos de Ação | spine by column (to do / in progress / done) |
| Initials avatar | Side menu, Configurações | dark green circle, 1–2 uppercase initials, two sizes (40px in the menu, 52px in Configurações) |
| AI persona card **[ext]** | Configurações | not selected (thin border) · selected (thick `#1F3D34` border + check icon) |
| Bar chart (dashboard) | Configurações | populated (10 bars) · one bar · empty (placeholder icon) |
| Export status card | Tela 4 (bottom sheet) | pending · processing · done · error · empty |
| Confirmation dialog | Sessão expirada, Confirmar exclusão | background scrim + centered card; neutral title (session) or red title (destructive deletion) |
| PIN keypad | Tela 0.1b/c | digits 0–9 + backspace; progress dots above |
| Tab bar | Insertion modal | 3 tabs (Texto/Áudio/Foto), active tab with filled background |
| Audio waveform | Insertion modal, Áudio tab | active/animated (recording) · frozen and faded (processing) |
| Skeleton | Any content loaded over the network | shown for calls longer than 300 ms (RNF01) |
